questions.stem: What is the scope of a variable declared inside a function?

options.text: Global scope
Local scope
Both local and global scope
No scope

questions.explanation: Variables declared inside a function have local scope, meaning they are only accessible within that function. They cannot be accessed outside the function.

questions.stem: Why can global variables make a program difficult to debug?

options.text: They are always constant.
They can be accessed and modified from anywhere in the program.
They are only accessible in the main function.
They have a short lifetime.

questions.explanation: Global variables can be accessed and modified from any part of the program, leading to unexpected changes and making it hard to track where and why a value was altered.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about local variables is true?

They are accessible only within the block where they are declared.

questions.explanation: The lifetime of a global variable is the duration of the program's execution. Since the program runs for 10 minutes, the global variable's lifetime is also 10 minutes.

questions.stem: What happens to a local variable when the function it is declared in returns?

options.text: It becomes a global variable.
It is destroyed and its memory is freed.
It retains its value for the next function call.
It is converted to a constant.

questions.explanation: When a function returns, all local variables declared within it are destroyed and their memory is freed. This is why their lifetime is limited to the function execution.
